title: {{NAME}} and the Princess Who Rode a Raptor
moral: A good ruler earns trust, and trust is built one courageous step at a time.

pages.content:
The palace had a problem.

In the royal stables, alongside the horses and the ceremonial elk, lived a Velociraptor named Duchess. Duchess had been there since the king was a boy, and nobody knew where she had come from, and nobody had ever managed to ride her.

Princess Isolde had tried. Six knights had tried. The royal veterinarian had tried and then retired.

Now {{NAME}}, the stable boy's apprentice, watched Duchess pace her enclosure and thought: she's not dangerous. She's bored.

pages.content:
He began leaving interesting things at the edge of her enclosure. A mirror. A ball. A complicated knot of rope.

Duchess ignored the mirror. She destroyed the ball in four seconds. The rope she spent forty minutes untying, then carried the end piece around for the rest of the day like a prize.

"She likes puzzles," {{NAME}} told Princess Isolde.

"Can you use that?" the princess asked, studying Duchess with calculating royal interest.

"I think so," said {{NAME}}. "But she has to choose to work with us. We can't force it."

pages.content:
The training took three weeks.

First: Duchess accepting food from {{NAME}}'s hand. Then from Princess Isolde's hand.

Then: following a rope course through the stable yard for food rewards.

Then: a saddle, no rider, just existing. Duchess wore it for a day with dignified disdain.

Then: {{NAME}} on her back for five minutes, then twenty, then an hour, while Duchess pretended she had decided to do this entirely of her own accord.

Then: Princess Isolde.

Duchess went still. Considered. Then walked forward.

pages.content:
The first ride outside the palace was at dawn.

Duchess moved like water over uneven ground, absolutely sure-footed, her head up, reading the landscape.

Princess Isolde sat very still on her back and said nothing for a long time.

Then she said: "She's magnificent."

"Yes," said {{NAME}}, running beside them on foot, slightly out of breath. "She just needed someone to figure out what she needed."

Duchess made a low sound, like a purr crossed with a growl, that they had come to understand meant she was pleased.

pages.content:
That evening, {{NAME}} locked up the stables and said goodnight to Duchess.

She pressed the top of her head briefly against his hand, which she had never done before, then turned and settled into her straw with her tail curled around her.

{{NAME}} walked home through the palace grounds under a full moon, thinking about the look on Princess Isolde's face at dawn, and the sound Duchess made when she was pleased, and how the best things took patience.

He fell asleep almost immediately, and dreamed of open meadows and the sound of something fast and magnificent running.
